changes.after: Safe navigation skips a method call when the value before it is nil.

before:
value&.upcase calls upcase when value is not nil and returns nil without the call when value is nil. For a String, upcase returns uppercase text.

With a real String receiver, upcase takes no explicit argument and returns new uppercase text; it does not modify the original string. Unlike the nil example below, this call actually runs the method.
```ruby
text = "map"
puts text.upcase
puts text
```
It prints:
```text
MAP
map
```
A non-nil object still must support the called method. false is not nil, so safe navigation does not skip a call on false.
result || "missing" replaces both nil and false with the fallback. That is a truthiness policy, not a universal missing-data rule.

Complete local Ruby example; the app itself does not execute it:
```ruby
value = nil
result = value&.upcase
puts result || "missing"
```
Expected output or behavior: missing. Compiler evidence is recorded separately from app reading completion.
